comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD describe their data center compute offerings as integrated stacks combining hardware accelerators with software optimization tools. NVDA explicitly lists 'energy efficient GPUs, DPUs, interconnects, and fully optimized AI and HPC software stacks' alongside specific software services like DGX Cloud. Similarly, AMD lists 'server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs' and states it leverages its technology to address 'AI workload acceleration needs' for a 'diverse set of workloads'. A key difference is that AMD's disclosure explicitly includes 'CPUs' and 'FPGAs' as core components of its data center portfolio alongside GPUs and AI accelerators, whereas NVDA's description in this specific sentence focuses on GPUs, DPUs, and interconnects as the hardware basis for its supercomputing platforms.

sentences.text: Our compute offerings include supercomputing platforms and servers, bringing together our energy efficient GPUs, DPUs, interconnects, and fully optimized AI and high-performance computing, or HPC, software stacks.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products.
We leverage our technology to address the computational, visual data processing and AI workload acceleration needs in the data center market.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops world-class software stacks, including tools, compilers, and drivers, and works with customers to define customized solutions using its IP and design leadership.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies emphasize the importance of their software ecosystems in supporting hardware performance. NVDA highlights 'NVIDIA AI Enterprise software', 'acceleration libraries, APIs, SDKs, and domain-specific application frameworks' as part of its compute offerings. AMD mirrors this by stating it develops 'world-class software stacks' including 'development tools, compilers, and drivers' to enable its products. While NVDA frames its software as part of the immediate compute product definition (including cloud services), AMD frames its software development as a foundational enabler that works with customers to define 'customized solutions' to match specific requirements.

sentences.text: In addition, they include NVIDIA AI Enterprise software; our DGX Cloud service; and a growing body of acceleration libraries, APIs, SDKs, and domain-specific application frameworks.
We develop world-class software stacks that are used to enable our high-performance products.
We work closely with our customers to define and develop customized solutions to precisely match their requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU address the specific hardware demands of AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads in the data center. NVDA describes its compute offerings as platforms bringing together GPUs and DPUs to serve AI/HPC needs. MU describes how 'applications such as machine learning servers require fast access to data' and highlights its SSDs (6500 and 9550 series) as solutions for 'AI data lake applications' and 'AI, high-performance computing'. The comparison highlights the complementary nature of compute (NVDA) and storage (MU) in the AI infrastructure stack, with both companies explicitly targeting the 'AI and high-performance computing' workload segment.
